initialContact.message: I'm 42 and my body is breaking down from factory work. My back hurts every day. I heard about something called 'varhaiseläke' (early retirement) but when I looked it up, it seems like it doesn't really exist anymore? There's disability pension but I'm not disabled - I can still work, it just hurts. Can I retire early somehow or am I stuck working until 65? That's another 23 years of pain.

problemContext.currentSituation: Factory worker with chronic pain exploring early retirement options, confused about what exists in current Finnish system
problemContext.emotionalState: frustrated, in physical pain, feeling trapped, hopeless

idealAdvice: Your frustration is completely understandable - physical work is hard on the body
You're right that traditional 'varhaiseläke' was eliminated in 2005 pension reform
BUT - several options still exist depending on your situation:
1. Työkyvyttömyyseläke (disability pension) - if medical evidence shows work capacity significantly reduced
2. Osittainen työkyvyttömyyseläke (partial disability pension) - can work reduced hours while receiving partial pension
3. Kuntoutustuki (rehabilitation support) - if you could retrain for less physical work
4. Osa-aikaeläke (part-time pension) - available from age 61 if born before 1965
Key: You don't have to be 'fully disabled' for disability pension - 'significantly reduced work capacity' is enough
Document your pain: regular doctor visits, specialists, physical therapy - medical records crucial
Occupational health doctor can assess if your current job is sustainable
Consider: Could you transition to lighter role in factory? Supervisor, quality control, training?
Kela has advisors who help navigate disability pension applications - free service
Your employer might have responsibility to offer adapted work if health limits current role
Don't suffer in silence for 23 years - explore your options NOW while you can still work
commonMistakes: Just telling him early retirement doesn't exist anymore without offering alternatives
Not explaining partial disability pension option
Dismissing his pain as 'just part of the job'
Not mentioning importance of medical documentation
Failing to suggest retraining or role modification options
Not acknowledging the emotional and physical toll
